title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: Single-arm phase II clinical trials commonly used evaluate whether new treatment agents sufficient antitumor activity warrant investigation randomized phase III trials. many trials use binary endpoints (e.g., tumor response), situations time--event (TTE) endpoints appropriate. vignette demonstrates use two_stage_single_arm_tte() function design optimal two-stage single-arm phase II trials time--event endpoints, based methodology Wu et al. (2020).

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: Time--event endpoints particularly useful : Cytostatic agents: Drugs prevent tumor growth may cause tumor shrinkage Molecularly targeted agents: Treatments may stabilize disease Immunotherapy: Treatments response may delayed Progression-free survival (PFS): Common oncology trials Event-free survival (EFS): Relevant many disease settings

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: design uses one-sample log-rank test (OSLRT) compare observed survival known null distribution. approach: Uses entire survival distribution (just single time point) Allows restricted follow-(practical clinical trials) Provides exact variance estimates adequate power Accommodates various survival distributions

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: Let’s reproduce design Wu et al. (2020) trial evaluating immunotherapy second-line treatment small-cell lung cancer patients. Background: - Historical data: median PFS = 3.5 months (Topotecan) - Treatment goal: improve median PFS 5 months - historical PFS follows Weibull distribution shape parameter 1.47327 Design parameters:
code: design <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(   shape = 1.47327,    # Weibull shape parameter   S0 = 0.5,           # Survival probability at 3.5 months (median)   x0 = 3.5,           # Time point for S0   hr = 0.5913,        # Hazard ratio (3.5/5)^1.47327   tf = 5,             # Follow-up duration (months)   rate = 2,           # Accrual rate (patients/month)   alpha = 0.05,       # Type I error (one-sided)   beta = 0.2,         # Type II error (80% power)   dist = "WB",        # Weibull distribution   restricted = FALSE  # Unrestricted follow-up model )  print(design) #> $param #>     shape  S0     hr alpha beta rate  x0 tf restricted #> 1 1.47327 0.5 0.5913  0.05  0.2    2 3.5  5      FALSE #>  #> $Single_stage #>   nsingle tasingle  csingle #> 1      42       21 1.644854 #>  #> $Two_stage #>   n1   c1  n     c  t1 MTSL      ES     PS #> 1  9 1.25 17 0.737 4.2 13.5 9.30816 0.8944

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: Longer follow-periods can reduce sample size requirements:
code: # 5 months follow-up design_5mo <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(   shape = 1.47327, S0 = 0.5, x0 = 3.5, hr = 0.5913,   tf = 5, rate = 2, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, dist = "WB",   restricted = FALSE )  # 10 months follow-up design_10mo <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(   shape = 1.47327, S0 = 0.5, x0 = 3.5, hr = 0.5913,   tf = 10, rate = 2, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, dist = "WB",   restricted = FALSE )  comparison <- data.frame(   Follow_up = c("5 months", "10 months"),   Total_n = c(design_5mo$Two_stage$n, design_10mo$Two_stage$n),   Stage1_n = c(design_5mo$Two_stage$n1, design_10mo$Two_stage$n1),   Expected_n = c(design_5mo$Two_stage$ES, design_10mo$Two_stage$ES) )  print(comparison)

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Designs for Time-to-Event Endpoints
text: ’s often useful examine design changes different assumptions:
code: hr_values <- seq(0.5, 0.8, by = 0.1) results <- data.frame(   Hazard_Ratio = hr_values,   Single_Stage_n = NA,   Two_Stage_n = NA,   Two_Stage_ES = NA )  for (i in seq_along(hr_values)) {   design <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(     shape = 1.47327, S0 = 0.5, x0 = 3.5, hr = hr_values[i],     tf = 5, rate = 2, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, dist = "WB",     restricted = FALSE   )   results$Single_Stage_n[i] <- design$Single_stage$nsingle   results$Two_Stage_n[i] <- design$Two_stage$n   results$Two_Stage_ES[i] <- design$Two_stage$ES }  print(results)

title: Sample Size, Power, and Simulation for Clinical Trial Designs
text: example reproduces design Wu et al. (2020) single-arm phase II trial evaluating immunotherapy second-line treatment small-cell lung cancer patients.
code: library(blueprint)  # Design parameters: # - Null hypothesis: median PFS = 3.5 months (Weibull distribution) # - Alternative: median PFS = 5 months (hazard ratio = 0.5913) # - Restricted follow-up: 5 months # - Accrual rate: 2 patients per month # - Type I error: 5%, Power: 80%  design <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(   shape = 1.47327,      # Weibull shape parameter   S0 = 0.5,             # Survival probability at x0 under H0   x0 = 3.5,             # Time point for S0 (median)   hr = 0.5913,          # Hazard ratio under H1   tf = 5,               # Follow-up time   rate = 2,             # Accrual rate (patients/month)   alpha = 0.05,         # Type I error (one-sided)   beta = 0.2,           # Type II error (80% power)   dist = "WB",          # Weibull distribution   restricted = FALSE    # Unrestricted follow-up (Wu et al. default) )  # View the design print(design)

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Design for Time-to-Event Endpoints — two_stage_single_arm_tte
text: shape Numeric. Shape parameter parametric survival distribution null hypothesis. S0 Numeric. Survival probability fixed time point x0 null hypothesis. x0 Numeric. Fixed time point S0 specified. hr Numeric. Hazard ratio alternative hypothesis (proportional hazards model). Values < 1 indicate improvement. x Numeric. Restricted follow-time period patient. rate Numeric. Constant accrual rate (patients per time unit). alpha Numeric. Type error rate (one-sided). Default 0.05. beta Numeric. Type II error rate. Default 0.2 (80% power). dist Character. Distribution null hypothesis. Options : "WB": Weibull distribution "LN": Log-normal distribution "GM": Gamma distribution "LG": Log-logistic distribution "SP": Logspline distribution (requires data argument) data Data frame. Required dist = "SP". Must contain columns time status fitting logspline distribution.

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Design for Time-to-Event Endpoints — two_stage_single_arm_tte
text: list three elements: param Data frame input parameters Single_stage Data frame single-stage design parameters: nsingle, tasingle, csingle Two_stage Data frame two-stage design parameters: n1, c1, n, c, t1, MTSL, ES, PS

title: Two-Stage Single-Arm Design for Time-to-Event Endpoints — two_stage_single_arm_tte
text: function implements optimal two-stage design algorithm described Wu, Chen, Wei, Weiss, Chauhan (2020). design allows early stopping futility first stage based one-sample log-rank test. design parameters : n1: Sample size stage 1 c1: Critical value stage 1 (stop Z1 ≤ c1) n: Total sample size c: Critical value final analysis (reject H0 Z > c) Four parametric distributions supported: Weibull: S(t) = exp(-(t/b)^) Log-normal: S(t) = 1 - Φ((log(t) - μ)/σ) Gamma: S(t) = 1 - I_a(t/b) Log-logistic: S(t) = 1/(1 + (t/b)^)
